hero_prop_criteria.center_of_focus: The story, a shot or a character's attention centres on the object.
hero_prop_criteria.high_frequency: The object is present in more than one scene/act.
hero_prop_criteria.transfer: The object passes between two characters.

scenes.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING

hero_props.name: Yonah’s small lunch
hero_props.description: Yonah’s five barley loaves and two fish, first carried as a small bundle, then offered to Jesus, multiplied, distributed, eaten, and gathered as leftovers. The multiplied bread and fish are treated as the same story prop changing form through the miracle.
hero_props.reason: This is the central miracle prop: characters debate whether it is enough, Yonah gives it away, Jesus receives it, it multiplies, and it is distributed through the crowd.

hero_props.name: honey-date cakes
hero_props.description: Miri’s three honey-date cakes, carried in a cloth bundle. They begin as guarded treats, become the object lesson Miri applies after the loaves-and-fish story, and are finally shared with Tav and Nim.
hero_props.reason: The cakes drive Miri’s generosity conflict, recur across the home-world scenes, are repeatedly discussed, and are physically given/shared in the resolution.

hero_props.name: miracle baskets
hero_props.description: The baskets used by the disciples and children to distribute the multiplied bread and fish and gather twelve baskets of leftovers.
hero_props.reason: The baskets become the visible measure of the miracle: passed through the crowd, handed to Miri, filled beyond expectation, and gathered as twelve full baskets.

hero_props.name: linen basket and folded linen
hero_props.description: The errand basket Ima gives Miri, containing folded linen for Saba’s patched sleeves. The basket also conceals the cakes and later becomes Nim’s resting place.
hero_props.reason: It is physically handed from Ima to Miri, recurs in multiple scenes, carries the cakes, and delivers the linen that motivates Miri’s visit to Saba.

hero_props.name: small loaves-and-fish scroll
aliases: drawing of five loaves and two fish
hero_props.description: Saba’s small scroll tied with a barley-colored cord and sealed with a loaf-and-two-fish mark. When opened, it becomes the portal-like storytelling object that carries Miri into the hillside story.
hero_props.reason: The scroll is the central storytelling prop: Saba selects it, opens it, its ink transforms into the Galilean hillside, and it remains glowing afterward.

hero_props.name: Tav’s broken toy cart
hero_props.description: Tav’s small broken cart with a loose wheel, first seen when Miri refuses him a cake and later repaired with Miri’s help using a small peg Nim noses toward her.
hero_props.reason: The cart is a recurring physical sign of Tav’s need and Miri’s missed chance to help; repairing it accompanies her final act of generosity. The repair peg is physically moved from Nim toward Miri.
